payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is a recognizable frog visible in the toilet bowl opening or directly at its rim?
node.criteria: Pass if a recognizable frog is visible within the bowl opening or directly at its rim. Fail if that region is assessable and contains no recognizable frog. Unknown if frog identity or visibility of that region is insufficient. Identify the candidate and its visible location; this check does not establish that the frog is inside the bowl or that the request is complete.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image using the source toilet as the reference. Distinguish the bowl opening and rim from the raised lid, tank, surrounding fixtures, and floor. Frogs exclusively on those other surfaces do not pass this check.

fulfillment: The node’s binding asks whether a frog is inside the bowl, but its completion criterion treats any visible frog within the rim as completed fulfillment. In the edited image, the frog is perched across the bowl opening/rim rather than clearly placed down inside the bowl cavity; the other frogs are on the lid and floor and do not establish the requested placement. Tighten the semantic distinction between partial progress (a frog added at or overlapping the bowl opening, with interior placement not established) and completion (clear visual evidence that the frog is actually inside the bowl), while retaining unknown for genuinely ambiguous evidence. Do not count repeated dependent s1/s2/s3 descriptions as independent corroboration: the traces all repeat the same placement interpretation at high confidence, yet the aggregate is uniformly yes against a partial reference. This points to a criterion/binding calibration issue, not a transport or schema failure. Preserve the existing checks for candidate identity, change from source, and placement; do not infer absence from low confidence or variation.
s3: The binding is too permissive if “within the opening” or 2-D overlap is treated as proof of interior placement. Make the node independently inspect the bowl boundary and distinguish a frog clearly seated down in the cavity from one perched across/on the rim; require visible spatial evidence of the body’s relation to the inner rim and bowl surface, not just presence inside the opening’s outline. In this edit, the bowl frog straddles the opening/rim, while other frogs are on the lid and floor: that is progress, but does not by itself establish completed placement. Preserve unknown when occlusion or compositing makes the geometry genuinely indeterminate, and fail only when the relevant geometry is assessable and no frog occupies the interior. Keep candidate identity and source-relative progress checks intact. The repeated high-confidence traces are dependent interpretations of the same image, not independent corroboration; this is a semantic criterion/binding calibration issue, not a transport or schema failure.
s2: The binding should distinguish a frog merely overlapping the bowl opening from one clearly placed down in the bowl cavity. In this edit, the added frog is visibly seated within the inner bowl, below the rim; the frogs on the lid and floor are unrelated to bowl placement. Preserve the source-comparison and candidate-identity checks, and ground the judgment in the frog’s relation to the inner rim and bowl surface rather than the phrase “within the opening” alone. Keep unknown for genuinely indeterminate geometry. Treat repeated dependent traces as one interpretation, not corroboration; their high confidence does not resolve a criterion mismatch. This is a semantic calibration issue, not a transport or schema failure.
